items.title: Session Management
items.content: A session is one full school year. Inside it, you create terms (subsessions) with real start and end dates. A session is active when the current date is inside the session start and end dates. In the same way, a term (subsession) is active when the current date is inside that term's start and end dates. Everything else — classes, enrollment, scores, and report cards — runs inside the active session and active term.

steps.step: How a session works (with real dates)
steps.desc: Think of a session as the whole school year, and terms as the parts of that year.

blocks.text: Think of a session as the whole school year, and terms as the parts of that year.
Example session: 2025/2026 — Start: 8 September 2025 — End: 24 July 2026. That date range is the full academic year.
Inside that same session, you create terms (subsessions). Example:
First Term: 8 September 2025 → 12 December 2025. Second Term: 12 January 2026 → 3 April 2026. Third Term: 20 April 2026 → 24 July 2026.

Rules that make this easy: every term date must sit inside the session dates. Terms should not overlap each other. When one term ends, the next term starts later — not on the same day as another active term.

What uses these dates: students enroll into a class for a session and term. Attendance, scores, and report cards belong to that term. When the year ends, you create a new session (for example 2026/2027) and promote students to the next class.

blocks.text: Click Create Session. Give it a clear name (for example 2025/2026), then set the real start and end dates for the whole school year — like 8 September 2025 to 24 July 2026. Save.

steps.desc: Open the session and add First Term, Second Term, and Third Term with their own start and end dates. Each term must fit inside the session dates.

blocks.text: Open the session and add First Term, Second Term, and Third Term with their own start and end dates. Each term must fit inside the session dates. For example, First Term cannot start before the session start date, and Third Term cannot end after the session end date.

items.callout: Simple rule: Session = full year dates. Terms = parts of that year. Term dates must stay inside the session. Use search when you have many sessions.

blocks.text: A session is one full school year. Inside it, you create terms (subsessions) with real start and end dates. A session is active when the current date is inside the session start and end dates. In the same way, a term (subsession) is active when the current date is inside that term's start and end dates. Everything else — classes, enrollment, scores, and report cards — runs inside the active session and active term.
Example: Session 2025/2026 runs from 8 September 2025 to 24 July 2026. First Term, Second Term, and Third Term sit inside those dates, one after another, without overlapping.
